alternatives.note: same level-preserving family, per-channel variant; k=3 validated. Lower than gamma_HSV:5 because V-gamma matches saturated sky (pair1) and dark colourful spiders (pair2) better.
R0 pipeline, cross-family shift fallback only; unique-level evidence (target ~241-252 vs shift sim ~155-166) argues against shift families.

analysis.mode: PSNR (noise_prior sigma 0.62/1.48/0.74 << noise_gaussian sev1 = 12.75 grey levels -> no random noise)

per_step_verdict.verdict: LIKELY on pair0 (43.97 dB), UNCERTAIN on pair1/pair2

analysis.rationale: R1 changes the global darkening from the V-shift family to brightness_darken_gamma_HSV:5 (V^3.5), the only family consistent with all signals: (1) target unique_R/G/B levels (248/252/241, 252/251/252, 252/251/250) are preserved, whereas every additive-shift simulation collapses them to ~155-166 (CI unique diff target-sim +82..+100); (2) target zero-clip fractions 0.669/0.264/0.137 match gamma sev5 near-zero thresholds (V<=49 for g=3.5, x<=45 for g=3.2) with residual clip diffs 0.2%/4%/8%, while RGB:5 over-clips pair1 by 16 pp; (3) a single V-gamma simultaneously explains mean_shift -45.3/-66.7/-74.4, variance_ratio 0.193/0.709/0.830 and chroma_ratio 0.289/0.620/0.393 without a second global step (sampler allows only one function per category); (4) pair0 reaches 43.97 dB (>40 dB = deterministic confirmation) with exact unique/clipping match, while R0's 34.58 dB for the shift family was inflated by 67% black clipping. Pair1 (24.45 dB) and pair2 (31.17 dB) remain below the deterministic ceiling; peeled residual after gamma_HSV:5 on pair1 is structured, not noise (residual_std 14.9, spatial_corr 0.651, cross_ch_corr 0.9959, ivc 0.9974, noise_prior sigma 4.94 << sev1; extreme_pct 75.5% meets the known >50% + sigma<5 FP rule). Target is slightly smoother than sim (hf_lf diff 25%, zero_crossing 39%), so an unmodelled mild blur is the leading residual explanation; blur+gamma combos could not be validated on k=3 within the call budget and are left for R2, not adopted here.
analysis.coupling_notes: The sampler (blind_challenge.py) allows at most one function per category, so brightness+saturation / brightness+contrast pipelines are impossible; the observed chroma loss must come from the single global function itself, which is exactly what V-gamma produces (chroma scales with V^(g-1)). The remaining pair1/pair2 residual is content-dependent (fine-detail scenes lose more) and points to a possible mild blur step (pair2 full_analysis flags glass: glass_score 0.2998, spectral_slope_ratio 1.0914, mtf_roughness 1.3616; pair0/pair1 do not reach blur thresholds).
analysis.k_limitation: k=3 support pairs only; no external data added. Pair0 is the primary alias (degraded.png).
